model.rationale: San Antonio's TX-20 leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent Joaquin Castro has outraised challenger Edgardo Baez by roughly ten to one. Prediction markets price Castro around 95%, consistent with the district's fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Baez or an unexpectedly strong Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though a Castro loss remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joaquin Castro seeks another term in a San Antonio-area district that voted about sixteen points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles. He is a well-known incumbent with a substantial campaign war chest, while Republican Edgardo Baez has raised only modest funds and lacks outside support. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so expectations rest on district fundamentals and fundraising.

Prediction markets give Castro roughly a 95% chance of winning, in line with the district's partisan lean and his incumbency. The forecast expects Castro to win comfortably, with some uncertainty from the absence of polling and the possibility of a favorable Republican environment.
